items.title: Adding Error Bars to Evals: A Statistical Approach to Language Model Evaluations
items.summary: Treats eval questions as draws from an unseen population of questions. Recommends CLT standard errors, clustered standard errors when questions share context, paired-difference tests when comparing models, resampling answers to reduce variance, and power analysis before running an eval.

items.title: A statistical approach to model evaluations
items.summary: Anthropic's plain-language companion to the error-bars paper, with five concrete recommendations for how labs should report eval results.

items.title: Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks
items.summary: Measures how much benchmark scores move across random seeds and training runs, shows many reported differences sit inside that noise, and tests whether techniques such as item response theory reduce it.

items.title: With Little Power Comes Great Responsibility
items.summary: Brings power analysis to NLP evaluation and finds many common experimental setups are too small to reliably detect the size of improvements papers typically report.

items.title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to Testing Statistical Significance in Natural Language Processing
items.summary: A practical guide to choosing a significance test for comparing two systems on the same test set, plus a survey of how rarely published papers actually test.

items.title: Chatbot Arena: An Open Platform for Evaluating LLMs by Human Preference
items.summary: Ranks models from crowdsourced pairwise votes using a Bradley–Terry model with confidence intervals, and studies how reliable crowd preferences are.

items.title: Chatbot Arena: New models & Elo system update
items.summary: LMSYS explains moving the leaderboard from online Elo updates to a Bradley–Terry fit with bootstrapped confidence intervals.

items.title: AI Agents That Matter
items.summary: Argues agent evaluations should report cost and accuracy together (a Pareto frontier), and flags overfitting to benchmarks and poor reproducibility in current agent evals.

items.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
items.summary: Measures how often strong LLM judges agree with human preferences, and documents judge biases such as position, verbosity, and self-enhancement.
items.venue: Zheng et al. · NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks

items.title: Judging the Judges: Evaluating Alignment and Vulnerabilities in LLMs-as-Judges
items.summary: Benchmarks many judge models against human annotators, compares agreement metrics, and probes where judges are easy to mislead.

items.title: Length-Controlled AlpacaEval: A Simple Way to Debias Automatic Evaluators
items.summary: Uses a regression adjustment to remove an automatic judge's preference for longer answers, a direct example of statistical debiasing of an evaluator.

items.title: Prediction-Powered Inference
items.summary: Builds valid confidence intervals by combining a small human-labeled set with many machine predictions, correcting for the predictor's bias.

items.title: AutoEval Done Right: Using Synthetic Data for Model Evaluation
items.summary: Applies prediction-powered inference to model evaluation: cheap model-generated labels plus a few human labels give unbiased, lower-variance accuracy estimates.

items.title: What Will it Take to Fix Benchmarking in Natural Language Understanding?
items.summary: Lays out criteria a benchmark should meet: validity, reliable annotation, enough statistical power, and not rewarding biased models.

items.title: Evaluation Examples are not Equally Informative: How should that change NLP Leaderboards?
items.summary: Uses item response theory to model how difficult and how discriminating each test item is, and argues leaderboards should account for this.

items.title: tinyBenchmarks: evaluating LLMs with fewer examples
items.summary: Uses item response theory to estimate full-benchmark performance from a small curated subset of items.

items.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
items.summary: Evaluates models across many scenarios and many metrics at once (accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, efficiency) instead of a single score.

items.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
items.summary: Introduces HumanEval and the unbiased pass@k estimator: sample n ≥ k attempts, count c correct, and estimate 1 − C(n−c, k) / C(n, k).

items.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
items.summary: Agent benchmark with simulated users and tools. Introduces pass^k, the chance an agent succeeds on all k independent tries, and shows consistency drops sharply as k grows.

items.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
items.summary: Fits a logistic curve of agent success against how long each task takes a human, and summarizes each model by its 50% time horizon.

items.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
items.summary: Agents must fix real GitHub issues, scored by running the repository's tests. A widely used agent benchmark and a good case study for test-based grading.

items.title: GAIA: a benchmark for General AI Assistants
items.summary: Questions that are simple for people but need tool use, browsing, and multi-step reasoning, graded by exact match against a short answer.

items.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
items.summary: Self-hosted websites where agents complete tasks, checked by programmatic validators of the final state.

items.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
items.summary: Evaluates LLMs as agents across eight environments, including operating system, database, and web tasks.

items.title: Inspect: an open-source framework for LLM and agent evaluations
items.summary: The UK AI Security Institute's eval framework. Useful for running your own agent evals with repeated epochs and built-in scorers.
